subtitle: When Sirhind Trembled: From Vengeance to Sovereignty

panels.shot: split composition with a low-angle view of Banda Singh Bahadur advancing through dust on one side and Wazir Khan rigid atop an elephant before Sirhind on the other
panels.action: Banda Singh Bahadur strides forward in battle-worn mail with sword drawn as Wazir Khan towers from a war elephant before the distant walls of Sirhind under a darkening May sky, two destinies rushing toward collision.

dialogue.text: In May 1710, a rebel saint and an imperial governor raced toward Chappar Chiri—and the fall of Sirhind would turn Sikh vengeance into open rule.

i18n.hi: मई १७१० में, एक बाग़ी फ़क़ीर और शाही सूबेदार चप्पर चिरी की तरफ़ दौड़े—सिरहिंद की हार ने सिख बदले को खुला राज बना दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Banda Singh Bahadur seated cross-legged, eyes closed, with a faint superimposed memory of young boys before Sirhind's walls behind him
panels.action: Banda Singh Bahadur sits in meditation under a tree, his face lined and still, while behind him the faint image of two young boys before the ramparts of Sirhind hangs like a shadow in the sky.

dialogue.text: Sikh chronicles tie this march to an older wound at Sirhind, where Guru Gobind Singh’s young sons were killed under Wazir Khan’s authority.

i18n.hi: सिख इतिहास सिरहिंद की इस चढ़ाई को पुरानी चोट से जोड़ते हैं, जहाँ गुरु गोबिंद सिंह के नन्हे साहिबज़ादे वज़ीर ख़ान की हुकूमत में मार डाले गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a dusty Punjab road with a mixed host moving forward, the camera slightly above and behind Banda at the head
panels.action: On a dusty road toward Sirhind, Banda Singh Bahadur rides at the head of a varied column—turbaned Sikhs with matchlocks, rough horsemen, barefoot peasants with spears, and camp followers trailing behind.

dialogue.text: Ganda Singh sees no vast army here, but a mixed force of devoted Sikhs, paid soldiers and irregular plunderers moving under one man’s command.

i18n.hi: गांदा सिंह यहाँ कोई विशाल फ़ौज नहीं देखते, बस समर्पित सिख, मज़दूरी के सिपाही और लुटेरे टोलों का मिला-जुला दल, सब एक ही सरदार के हुक्म में।

panels.shot: intercut medium shot: Banda addressing followers in a village square, and Wazir Khan reading a farman in his court
panels.action: In a village square, Banda Singh Bahadur addresses gathered Sikhs and villagers with a raised hand, while in Sirhind’s court Wazir Khan sits on a low throne listening as a scribe reads a royal farman aloud.

dialogue.text: Sikh sources frame Banda’s march as retribution for Sirhind, while Mughal records name it rebellion against the emperor’s order and his governor, Wazir Khan.

i18n.hi: सिख स्रोत बंदा की चढ़ाई को सिरहिंद पर बदला बताते हैं, जबकि मुग़ल रोजनामचे इसे बादशाह और उसके सूबेदार वज़ीर ख़ान के ख़िलाफ़ बग़ावत लिखते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a small fortified town under attack at dawn, seen from above; smoke rising as armed men pour in through a broken gate
panels.action: At dawn a small fortified town on the road burns at the edges as Banda Singh Bahadur’s men surge through a shattered gate, defenders fleeing down narrow lanes while villagers watch from doorways.

dialogue.text: On the march, contemporary accounts agree, towns loyal to Sirhind were stormed and plundered, as discipline and vengeance pulled in different directions.

i18n.hi: यात्रा के दौरान, समकालीन बयान मानते हैं कि सिरहिंद-परस्त कस्बे तोड़े और लूटे गए, जहाँ अनुशासन और बदला अलग-अलग दिशाओं में खींच रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside Wazir Khan’s audience hall, low angle on him as he gestures sharply to officers before a map
panels.action: Within Sirhind’s audience hall, Wazir Khan leans forward over a spread map, rings flashing as he points toward Chappar Chiri, officers around him tensed and attentive.

dialogue.text: In Sirhind, Wazir Khan gathered imperial contingents and allied chiefs, determined to crush the rising before it reached his walls.

i18n.hi: सिरहिंद में वज़ीर ख़ान ने शाही टुकड़ियाँ और रजवाड़ों को जुटाया, पक्का इरादा कि ये उठान उसकी दीवारों तक पहुँचने से पहले कुचल दी जाए।

panels.shot: broad landscape shot of Chappar Chiri plain at first light, two armies faintly visible assembling on opposite ridges
panels.action: Under a pale May dawn at Chappar Chiri, two hosts take shape on low ridges facing each other across a bare plain, banners lifting in the slow morning wind.

dialogue.text: Neither Sikh nor Mughal record gives a neutral, detailed eye-witness of this field, but both agree: here Wazir Khan met Banda Singh Bahadur in open battle.

i18n.hi: न सिख, न मुग़ल कोई तटस्थ, बारीक आँखों देखा हाल छोड़ते हैं, पर दोनों मानते हैं: यहीं वज़ीर ख़ान ने बंदा सिंह बहादुर से खुली जंग लड़ी।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on Banda Singh Bahadur on horseback, sword raised, dust swirling, with a sea of faces behind him
panels.action: Banda Singh Bahadur, mail glinting and eyes steady, raises his sword from horseback as dust curls around him and the mixed mass of his followers press close behind.

dialogue.speaker: banda_singh_bahadur_and_wazir_khan
dialogue.text: Stand firm. Today, Sirhind will hear our answer.

i18n.hi: डटे रहो। आज सिरहिंद हमारा जवाब सुनेगा।

panels.shot: high-angle wide shot of the battle lines clashing, with special focus on Wazir Khan atop an elephant in the center
panels.action: Across the Chappar Chiri plain, mounted archers and infantry collide in swirling lines while, at the Mughal center, Wazir Khan towers on a war elephant, standard raised above him.

dialogue.text: Later Mughal and Sikh narratives alike place Wazir Khan high on an elephant, the visible heart of Sirhind’s power on that field.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल और सिख दोनों बाद की दास्तानें वज़ीर ख़ान को हाथी पर ऊँचा दिखाती हैं—मैदान पर सिरहिंद की शक्ति का चलता दिल।

panels.shot: tight, dynamic mid-shot of Sikhs charging toward the elephant under a hail of arrows, camera placed at their shoulder height
panels.action: With arrows darkening the air, turbaned Sikh fighters rush forward in a tight knot toward Wazir Khan’s elephant, faces set and mouths open in silent cries as they close the distance.

dialogue.text: The chroniclers differ in detail, but converge on this: the Sikh charge drove through the imperial lines toward the governor’s mount.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार बारीकियों में अलग हैं, पर यहाँ मिलते हैं: सिख धावा शाही सफ़ों को चीरता सूबेदार के हाथी तक जा लगा।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot from slightly below of Wazir Khan on the elephant as armed men reach its flanks, the moment before the killing blow
panels.action: Wazir Khan grips his sword atop the swaying elephant as armed Sikh fighters swarm around the animal’s legs, one climbing the howdah edge with arm drawn back for a decisive strike.

dialogue.text: In the crush and dust, Wazir Khan was brought down and killed—both traditions mark his death here as the breaking of Sirhind’s will.

i18n.hi: धूल और धक्के में, वज़ीर ख़ान गिराया गया और मारा गया—दोनों परंपराएँ उसकी मौत को यहीं सिरहिंद की हिम्मत टूटने का लम्हा मानती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Mughal line collapsing, men and elephants turning away, viewed from behind Banda’s advancing riders
panels.action: From behind Banda Singh Bahadur’s advancing horsemen, the viewer sees Mughal troops scattering, some dropping weapons as elephants wheel away and the ordered line dissolves into flight.

dialogue.text: With their governor dead, Sirhind’s forces broke; what had begun as suppression of rebels turned into a rout on the plain of Chappar Chiri.

i18n.hi: सूबेदार के जाते ही सिरहिंद की फ़ौजें बिखर गईं; बग़ावत दबाने निकली जंग चप्पर चिरी के मैदान में भगदड़ बन गई।

panels.shot: distant view of Sirhind’s walls from a rise, with smoke from Chappar Chiri still faint behind, Banda’s force approaching in the foreground
panels.action: From a low hill, Banda Singh Bahadur and his commanders gaze toward the stout walls and domes of Sirhind, the faint smoke of Chappar Chiri lingering behind as their host moves down toward the city.

dialogue.text: After Chappar Chiri, the road lay open; Sikh and Mughal accounts agree that Banda turned at once toward the city that had long overshadowed the region.

i18n.hi: चप्पर चिरी के बाद राह खुल गई; सिख और मुग़ल दोनों मानते हैं कि बंदा सीधा उसी शहर की ओर मुड़ा जो बरसों से सूबे पर छाया हुआ था।

panels.shot: wide, slightly elevated shot of Sirhind’s gate under assault, with sections of wall burning and crowds rushing inside
panels.action: Sirhind’s great gate strains under the blows of rams and ladders as parts of the wall burn; inside the arch, townsfolk and soldiers push through narrow streets in panic as Banda’s men pour in.

dialogue.text: The fall of Sirhind was swift and violent; contemporary traditions speak of a city stormed, sacked and, in large part, razed.

i18n.hi: सिरहिंद का पतन तेज़ और ख़ूनी था; उस दौर की दास्तानें एक ऐसे शहर को याद करती हैं जो तूफ़ान की तरह फतह, लूटा और बड़ी हद तक जला डाला गया।

panels.shot: moody street-level shot inside Sirhind after the sack, with blackened buildings, toppled gateways and scattered goods
panels.action: In the aftermath, blackened walls lean over a street of broken doors and scattered chests, a toppled gateway lying askew while a few figures pick their way through the wreckage of Sirhind.

dialogue.text: Sikh sources remember Sirhind’s destruction as vengeance and justice; Mughal reports record it as the shocking ruin of a major provincial capital.

i18n.hi: सिख रिकॉर्ड सिरहिंद की बरबादी को बदला और इंसाफ़ मानते हैं; मुग़ल रिपोर्ट इसे एक बड़े सूबाई दारुल-हुकूमत की हैरान कर देने वाली तबाही लिखती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Banda Singh seated outdoors with peasants kneeling before him, a landlord’s house in the background marked and guarded
panels.action: Outside a seized landlord’s house, Banda Singh Bahadur sits on a simple chair as peasants in coarse cloth kneel before him, armed men standing guard by a doorway marked with a rough symbol.

dialogue.text: In the months after Sirhind’s fall, evidence points to new orders—land redistributed, some zamindari claims overturned, as Banda sought to recast power in the countryside.

i18n.hi: सिरहिंद गिरने के बाद के महीनों में सबूत दिखाते हैं नए फ़रमान—ज़मीनें बाँटी गईं, कुछ ज़मींदारियों के दावे पलटे, बंदा ने देहात की सत्ता नया आकार देने की कोशिश की।

panels.shot: tight overhead shot of a hammer striking a coin die, with the new coin lying beside older Mughal coins
panels.action: A hammer comes down on a metal die, sparks leaping, while beside the anvil a fresh coin bearing the Deg-Tegh-Fateh legend lies next to older Mughal coins on the workbench.

dialogue.text: Banda Singh Bahadur’s Deg-Tegh-Fateh coins—still found today—proclaimed in metal that a new sovereignty, not just a band of raiders, now claimed the land.

i18n.hi: बंदा सिंह बहादुर के ‘दег-तेग-फ़तेह’ सिक्के—जो आज भी मिलते हैं—धातु में ऐलान करते हैं कि अब सिर्फ़ लुटेरों का झुंड नहीं, नई हकूमत ज़मीन माँग रही है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Banda standing at dusk on Sirhind’s ruined wall, looking toward the distance, with a faint silhouette of marching imperial forces on the horizon
panels.action: At dusk Banda Singh Bahadur stands upon a broken stretch of Sirhind’s wall, cloak stirring as he looks toward a distant line of marching troops faint on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Yet the empire he had struck was not broken; soon, imperial forces would close in, and this first Sikh state would face relentless counter-attack.

i18n.hi: पर जिस सल्तनत पर उसने चोट की थी, वो टूटी नहीं; जल्द ही शाही फ़ौजें घिर आईं, और यह पहला सिख राज लगातार जवाबी हमलों में घिर गया।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from a commemorative pillar at Chappar Chiri, blending into a stylised map of Punjab marked with Sirhind, Chappar Chiri and later Sikh centres
panels.action: A lone commemorative pillar rises on the plain of Chappar Chiri; as the view pulls back, it blends into a stylised map of Punjab where Chappar Chiri, Sirhind and later Sikh centres glow faintly.

dialogue.text: Chappar Chiri and the fall of Sirhind show how memory hardens where punishment and power meet, turning a single campaign into the first bold line of Sikh sovereignty on the map.

i18n.hi: चप्पर चिरी और सिरहिंद का पतन दिखाते हैं कैसे यादें सख़्त हो जाती हैं जहाँ सज़ा और ताक़त मिलते हैं, और एक ही मुहिम नक्शे पर सिख राज की पहली गहरी लकीर बन जाती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Sirhind Trembled: From Vengeance to Sovereignty
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब सिरहिंद कांपा: बदले से राज तक
